This role ensures designs are safe, compliant, constructible, reliable, and aligned with operational, business, and site requirements. The Project Engineer partners with engineering disciplines, architects, project managers, facilities teams, EHS professionals, contractors, and external design firms throughout the project lifecycle. This position requires travel to project sites and organizational locations to support project development, design reviews, field assessments, construction activities, commissioning, and stakeholder engagement. Serve as the technical lead for civil and structural engineering requirements, design standards, specifications, and project execution. Develop and review civil and structural design criteria, calculations, drawings, specifications, scopes of work, and engineering studies. Support projects involving site development, grading, drainage, stormwater management, roads, parking areas, underground utilities, foundations, structural steel, concrete, and building modifications. Evaluate existing site and structural conditions; identify constraints, risks, and required remediation or reinforcement measures. Review engineering design packages for technical quality, code compliance, constructability, maintainability, safety, and alignment with project requirements. Coordinate with architectural, mechanical, electrical, process, environmental, and facility engineering disciplines to ensure integrated project solutions. Lead technical aspects of capital projects from feasibility and concept development through detailed design, construction, commissioning, and turnover. Travel as needed to support site assessments, project meetings, design workshops, construction reviews, inspections, commissioning, and operational-readiness activities. Provide technical support during construction, including field observations, resolution of design issues, review of contractor submittals, and evaluation of change requests. Ensure projects comply with applicable building codes, structural standards, civil design requirements, permitting obligations, and environmental regulations. Support the development and maintenance of civil and structural engineering standards, specifications, guidelines, and standard details. jobs.description: Career Category Engineering Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease–we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. What you will do Let’s do this! Let’s change the world! Do you want to help shape the future of biopharmaceutical manufacturing? Are you interested in working with a diverse product portfolio of life changing products in a dynamic working environment? Would you like to work with a highly motivated team of process science professionals to positively impact patients’ lives? Amgen discovers, develops and delivers innovative human therapeutics. A biotechnology pioneer since 1980, Amgen was one of the first companies to realize the new science’s promise by bringing safe, effective medicines from lab, to manufacturing plant, to patient. Advancing science and helping patients – these dual passions are ingrained in our culture. They drive our work, our values, and everything we do at Amgen. For staff around the world, our mission to serve patients and our commitment to science makes Amgen a place where we can make a positive difference in people’s lives while pursuing a challenging and fulfilling career. To foster a setting in which all staff may excel, we support a variety of growth opportunities, from training and education to expanding current job responsibilities. Amgen is seeking an Engineer to join the Drug Substance Technology & Engineering (DSTE) team at our Thousand Oaks, California site. In this onsite role, you will provide downstream purification process engineering support for a diverse portfolio of both clinical and commercial biologics drug substance products across the network. The Engineer will provide technology transfer, process validation, and manufacturing support for human therapeutic products (biological drug substance) in clinical development through commercial production. Our mission is to translate developmental processes to commercial reality for patients through scientific expertise and engineering innovation. You will work as a member of a team of engineers and scientists, as you use engineering principles to implement manufacturing processes in a cGMP environment. The successful candidate will apply process engineering knowledge in support of technology transfer and clinical and commercial drug substance manufacturing at Amgen’s Thousand Oaks site. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: · Transfer purification drug substance processes and process improvements from the laboratory to manufacturing facilities and between manufacturing sites. · Provide solutions to technical problems of moderate scope and complexity. · Evaluate, select, and apply standard engineering techniques and procedures under general supervision; seek assistance when addressing unusual problems. · Support process validation for late-stage commercial processes. · Provide on-the-floor technical support for process scale-up and technology transfer, as well as clinical and commercial manufacturing operations. · Perform routine and nonroutine process monitoring and troubleshooting. · Support nonstandard shift schedules and extended hours as business needs require. · Trend process data and perform statistical analyses. · Provide technical input for process-related deviations (NCs), CAPAs, and change controls. · Identify and support process-related operational excellence and continuous improvement opportunities, including efforts to improve efficiency across business process workstreams. · Represent Process Development and collaborate with Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Research, Maintenance, Utilities, Facilities, and Validation teams to develop requirements and recommendations for process or system modifications. · Communicate and collaborate with technical and management staff across Manufacturing, Process Development, and Quality. · Complete assignments with clear objectives that require investigating a limited number of variables. · Serve as a technical expert for equipment and systems troubleshooting, becoming actively involved in daily operations as needed to meet schedules or resolve complex problems. · Apply engineering principles and statistical methods, including design of experiments, to resolve processing issues and evaluate process improvement opportunities. Your work will improve security, reliability, and the employee experience. We’re looking for people who are passionate about automation, endpoint security, and building scalable solutions that improve employee experience. You should have deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets at scale, with strong software engineering skills to automate security controls and fleet operations across environments with different compliance requirements. Your problem-solving mindset and attention to detail will be key to success in this role. cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Manager, PDS BI&T Analytics Operations opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Brand Insights, Measurement Lead
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Brand Insights, Measurement Lead at Anthropic, you will strengthen the evidence that fuels our brand decisions: knowing whether marketing spend and effort is working, saying so clearly on a schedule to the people who need to hear it. Marketing Insights turns market, campaign and user data into decisions that product, marketing, comms and sales leadership can act on. You'll tell us, with data, whether awareness is turning into consideration, whether consideration is turning into pipeline, and where that chain breaks down for a given audience. This role sits at the intersection of human understanding, marketing science discipline and organizational influence. In this role, you'll own the team's recurring measurement readouts, including the Prosumer and B2B brand health tracker studies and the metrics, headwinds and tailwinds that show up in front of business leadership and in all-hands updates, keeping them accurate, current and easy to act on. You'll partner closely with your Marketing Insights teammates, Comms and data science on the brand-health dashboard, Brand & Integrated Marketing leadership, brand data science, research vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders across Enterprise Marketing, product marketing and finance. Responsibilities Own the recurring executive and all-hands readouts that put key metrics, headwinds and tailwinds in front of marketing management and the broader team Lead process ownership of the Prosumer and B2B brand health tracker studies, including managing the research vendor relationships that field them Lead coordination across Comms, Marketing and data science on the brand-health dashboard, aligning all three groups on one consistent view of the data Support media mix modeling, multi-touch attribution and incrementality analyses that inform how marketing budget and effort get allocated, moving the team past correlation to a defensible read on what's actually driving outcomes Run best-practice pre- and post-campaign analysis on individual campaigns, covering creative, channel, audience, and timing effects, and turn each read into a specific change for the next campaign Roll up campaign-level learnings into a recurring view for leadership: which channels, creative approaches, and audiences are outperforming over time, and where the team should adjust the playbook next Build audience and funnel analyses that quantify how different audiences move, and relate to each other, from awareness through consideration to conversion, and what that means for where to invest Audit how customer sentiment gets reported across the business and design a more efficient, consistent process Manage the underlying data pipelines so that recurring readouts stay reliable and don't get rebuilt from scratch each cycle Partner with Marketing Insights teammates to keep measurement process and research design in sync, including feeding into the Marketing Business Review scorecard process Develop one defensible view from first-party behavioral data, campaign and media data, and survey or attitudinal research, being clear about what each source can and can't tell you on its own Present findings to non-technical audiences, including marketing leadership, enterprise sales and finance partners, translating hedged results into clear recommendations You may be a good fit if you Have a strategic orientation, strong curiosity for understanding what customers and users think and how to shift perceptions, and can use that to influence business and marketing direction Are fluent in SQL and Python or R, and move comfortably between a quick exploratory pull and a more rigorous statistical model Have designed or analyzed experiments (A/B tests, holdouts, lift tests) to establish a causal effect rather than settle for a correlation, and have applied regression, segmentation or other causal-inference methods to a real business question Have run campaign-level measurement end to end, from a pre/post read on a single campaign to synthesizing learnings across multiple campaigns into a change the team acts on next time Have built and maintained a recurring metrics report or dashboard that executives or cross-functional partners actually rely on, and kept it trustworthy over time Can turn a hedged, caveated finding into a clear recommendation a non-technical stakeholder can act on, and know which caveat matters enough to keep in the headline Start an analysis by pinning down the business question and the decision it needs to serve, not the method that's most interesting to run Can reconcile data with no universal taxonomy across first-party, third-party, real-time and survey sources Know when a directionally correct answer now beats a more rigorous one that arrives too late to matter Work well across functions, building credibility with both technical partners and non-technical leadership Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial Strong candidates may also have Experience with media mix modeling, multi-touch attribution or incrementality and lift testing specifically, rather than general-purpose analytics Experience advising marketing stakeholders on experimental design for live campaigns (email, paid social), or measuring marketing performance across multiple markets Familiarity with survey-based quantitative research (MaxDiff, conjoint, brand and sentiment tracking) alongside behavioral and usage data Experience with a modern data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) and a BI tool (Tableau, Looker, Power BI) Prior experience in marketing, growth or brand analytics specifically, rather than data science in a general or product context A graduate degree in statistics, economics or another quantitative field A career trajectory spanning BI and dashboarding, applied causal inference and experimental design, and multi-market marketing measurement The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $255,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Dear Moderna Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate II, Quality Control, Stability opportunity with Moderna at Moderna.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

jobs.title: IT Lead
jobs.description: ABOUT US: AI NEEDS A NEW INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. WE'RE BUILDING IT AT MODAL. Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now. Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp https://modal.com/blog/how-ramp-built-a-full-context-background-coding-agent-on-modal, Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale. We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation. Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g.,Seaborn https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn,Luigi https://github.com/spotify/luigi), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience. ABOUT THE ROLE: We’re looking for our first IT Lead to build and own the systems that enable everyone at Modal to work effectively and securely. You’ll own our employee technology environment end-to-end, including identity and access, devices, internal systems, SaaS applications, and day-to-day IT operations. You’ll work closely with Security and Engineering to build an environment that is secure by default, easy to operate, and scales with the company. This is initially a hands-on role. You’ll build systems, automate workflows, and solve problems directly. As Modal grows, you’ll define how the IT function should scale and eventually build a team around it. WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON: Identity & Access - Own employee identity and access across internal systems and SaaS applications - Build scalable onboarding, offboarding, and access lifecycle workflows - Improve SSO, MFA, least privilege, and access management in partnership with Security Devices & Endpoints - Own the lifecycle and security of employee devices - Build and maintain device management, configuration, patching, and endpoint security - Automate provisioning and make onboarding as close to zero-touch as possible Internal Systems & Automation - Own and improve the SaaS applications and internal systems we depend on - Build integrations and automate workflows across identity, HR, finance, and other business systems - Evaluate and deploy new internal capabilities, including AI tools and integrations - Use APIs, scripting, and internal tooling to solve problems that don’t fit neatly into off-the-shelf products IT Operations - Own employee support, hardware, asset management, procurement, and relevant vendor relationships - Build reliable, maintainable processes rather than scaling through manual work - Identify recurring problems and solve them at the system level Build the IT Function - Define the technical direction and operating model for IT at Modal - Establish the systems and processes we’ll need as the company grows - Determine when and where additional IT capacity is needed, and build the team over time WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR: - Experience owning IT or corporate technology in a fast-growing technology company - Strong understanding of identity, device management, SaaS administration, and endpoint security - Strong technical skills and comfort working with APIs, scripting, automation, and system integrations - Experience designing and automating employee lifecycle and access-management workflows - Good security judgment and experience working closely with Security and Engineering - Ability to independently identify problems, make pragmatic technical decisions, and drive them through implementation - Comfortable being hands-on today while building the systems and team needed as the company grows

jobs.title: SoC Engineer
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems. This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces. - Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality. - Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components. - Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior. - Incorporate debug, test, and security requirements into the SoC architecture and implementation, partnering with other silicon designers to make the silicon observable, testable, and secure. - Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity. - Contribute to power management and security architecture and design. - Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up. - Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up. - Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality. - Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up. - Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB. - Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP. - Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links. - Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution. - Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery. - Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system. - Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable. - Enjoy stretching into multiple domains, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and rolling up your sleeves to build and debug. - Enjoy working on a small, dynamic team where priorities evolve and engineers take broad ownership. - Are excited about creatively applying automation and AI tools to hardware design and integration work. cold_email.subject: Interest in Lab Associate — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lab Associate opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Science & Engineering Rotational Graduate Programme 2027
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Science & Engineering Rotational Graduate Programme 2027 At Bristol Myers Squibb, we are inspired by a single vision: transforming patients’ lives through science. Bristol Myers Squibb is a leading global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with serious diseases. We combine the agility of a biotechnology company with the reach and resources of an established pharmaceutical organisation. Located in Dublin, the Cruiserath Biologics Campus is a key part of the Bristol Myers Squibb global manufacturing network. The campus includes an established multi-product biologics drug substance manufacturing operation, global biologics testing capabilities and a major expansion through the new Sterile Drug Product (SDP) facility. The SDP investment will add sterile drug product manufacturing and laboratory capabilities, supporting existing medicines and future pipeline assets. Its scope includes product formulation, component preparation, aseptic filling and capping of liquid and freeze-dried vials, aseptic syringe filling, visual inspection, clean utilities and the supporting quality, engineering, digital, supply chain and operational-readiness systems. Our rotational graduate offering is a major step towards a career that you will find fulfilling, both professionally and personally. The programme is structured around three nine-month rotations across relevant Science, Engineering and business functions. Rotations are matched with graduate development goals and business needs, providing broad experience across the Cruiserath Campus and opportunities to contribute to both established biologics operations and the delivery, start-up and ongoing operation of the new SDP facility. As a Science or Engineering Graduate, you will work with experienced technical teams, senior management and business leaders. Depending on your rotations, you may support cross-functional activities in areas such as Manufacturing, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Quality, Engineering, Commissioning, Qualification and Validation, Computer Systems Validation, Automation, Supply Chain, Operational Excellence and Project Management. You will contribute to meaningful projects, develop an understanding of the regulated biopharmaceutical environment and build the technical, digital and interpersonal capabilities required for a long-term career at Bristol Myers Squibb. The team partners with business stakeholders and the CRM team, routing technical defects and system development needs to the appropriate IT or product teams. MAIN REPONSIBILITIES: Demonstrate medical and scientific leadership and expertise Ensure the highest scientific standards during in / external activities to provide deep medical and scientific expertise. Develop local medical plan aligned with global medical plan to address local unmet medical needs and fill data gaps, and contribute to the implementation of local medical strategies and life cycle clinical plans for inline and pipeline medicines / vaccines. JOB DESCRIPTION Acquire and maintain extensive, up-to-date medical and pharmaceutical information in the assigned area to identify unmet needs and support medical strategy. Optimize patient centricity of medical communications and deliverables, incorporating Health Literacy and cultural awareness principles to ensure that patients remain the ultimate focus. Establish deep and enduring peer-to-peer scientific relationships with leading HCPs and specialists, including non-traditional partners and key decision makers. Maintain and enhance the cross-BU alignment on metrics. Ensure to collect necessary information and analyze insights prior to the meetings to provide deep medical and scientific expertise to stakeholders and HCPs. Aligns, contributes, and collaborates with Relevant internal stakeholders Provide information on expert / HCP / relevant feedback on product life cycle strategies to related divisions/department in the company. Share the medical/scientific information & insights within appropriate limits/ways for Marketing colleagues to develop brand plan(s). Scientific input for scientific meetings and materials Provide medical education programs with medical societies or relevant stakeholders. Collaboration in clinical development Provide medical/scientific input into protocol feasibility assessments for clinical trial proposals. Collaborate with Development Japan (DJ)/global development to identify appropriate investigators / sites for Pfizer-sponsored clinical trials. Work together with clinical research/DJ colleagues and in collaboration with above country and global BU colleagues to drive the timely completion of Pfizer-sponsored clinical trials. Demonstrate scientific / medical leadership and provide input into the global clinical teams and DJ to ensure design and selection of trials relevant to Japan’s needs, leveraging customer and patient insights Supporting DJ on clinical development program as well as regulatory interactions from early development phase. Contribute to the development and implementation of product(s)/therapeutic area(s) medical strategy and delivering medical and scientific advice both internally and externally to assure appropriate use of product(s) and patient’s safety aligned with the short- and long-term business goals of assigned product(s)/therapeutic area(s). Data communication and customer insights Provide accurate, high-quality, and unbiased medical information to HCPs and external experts, including managing unsolicited medical requests (UMRs). Provide scientific insight and support to field- and head office based commercial colleagues. Collaborate with the cross functional team in-country and above-country to develop impactful and compliant promotional and non-promotional materials of value to customers. If media-trained, present the scientific perspective on selected topics during media-briefings. Observe the code of conduct, company’s regulations, and compliance, make communication with related departments, and exercise leadership in POJ. Ensure awareness of code of contact for Medical Affairs (guidance for external medical interactions) and observe it. Give promotional or non-promotional explanations depending on the related departments. Conduct activities in compliance with the MHLW Guidelines for Prescription Drug Sales Information Activities. JOB DESCRIPTION Ensure activities and communications are conducted in compliance with all policies, guidelines, and regulations. Ensure awareness of responsibility for reporting adverse events For all Pfizer products, observe applicable laws/regulations and the Pfizer policy, and “Gather and report safety information*.” At an appropriate time, attend training programs on obligation of assigned safety reporting. AS NEEDED: Contribute to Business Development in the assigned area(s): In collaboration with Japan Medical Lead, Japan Medical Product Lead, Global MA members and other members from relevant functions, identify unmet medical needs and candidate therapies for potential medical interventions in the assigned therapeutic area(s) in Japan through medical activities such as advisory boards and consultations with medical experts while keeping confidentiality. Rapidly respond to critical supply issues from a medical perspective (e.g., rapid communications with academic societies and regulatory authorities). Collaborate effectively with teams and across functions by demonstrating Pfizer’s Values & Behaviors and the agility to learn from others. Capable of medical discussion with relevant departments and external HCPs. A person who understands compliance and relevant laws/regulations in the pharmaceutical industry and advocates the appropriate use of the products. Can demonstrate appropriate knowledge and understanding of internal organization structure, key stakeholders and strategies. A person who can quickly acquire necessary medical/ scientific knowledge and skills through self-learning. Experience: MA/DJ experience and / or research experience preferred. JOB DESCRIPTION Scientific publication experience preferred. Language: Able to understand written and spoken English and Japanese in assigned therapeutic disease area, and scientific interactions. Minimum TOEIC score of 730 Pfizer is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity legislation in each jurisdiction in which it operates. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Inference
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic’s Inference organization serves Claude to millions of users and enterprise customers, across our own products and the world’s largest cloud platforms, with the speed, reliability, and efficiency that frontier AI demands. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, an in-house inference engine that manages the entire token path for both production and research workloads, distributed routing, autoscaling, and capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation. We build across GPUs, TPUs, and Trainium, and the complexity of building, testing, and shipping inference software grows with every platform we add. We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the programs that scale it. The work spans four closely coupled areas: Scaling and infrastructure. Routing, autoscaling, and capacity management for the serving fleet, and bringing new capacity online. Velocity. The toolchains, development environments, and CI/CD that let inference engineers build, test, and ship across every accelerator platform. Inference engine. The software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer that serves every request. Performance. Improving throughput, latency, cost, and reliability across the stack, with correctness treated as part of performance. This is not a status-tracking role. You'll own outcomes end to end, often where no single team is accountable for the whole picture. Much of your value comes from crossing boundaries into Research, Safeguards, Security, Compute, Infrastructure, API, and our cloud and silicon partners, and bringing back the requirements and dependencies that no team sees from inside its own space. There is little process to inherit, and we want to keep it that way: you'll build the minimum machinery the work needs and remove it when it stops helping. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator. We expect TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management and fleet operations can look like. Key responsibilities Own the programs that scale Claude’s serving fleet across accelerator and cloud platforms, from early direction through delivery. Drive new capacity online end to end, working across compute, infrastructure, security, networking, and inference teams so one person is accountable for the whole path. Build visibility into supply, demand, and utilization with capacity and finance partners, and drive trade-offs among utilization, cost, latency, and reliability to a clear decision. Lead reliability programs and large migrations without disrupting production traffic or research, and make sure incident follow-ups land in team roadmaps. Drive the programs that make inference engineers faster: define the productivity metrics that matter, find the bottlenecks, and improve how software is built, tested, and released across platforms, in step with Anthropic’s central Infrastructure org. Coordinate roadmaps and priorities across the production, research, and safeguards needs that depend on the same teams. Track performance and efficiency work from opportunity to measured impact in production, with correctness held as a release criterion. Own inference readiness for model launches alongside our launch TPMs. Minimum qualifications 7+ years of experience as a TPM, or in an equivalent engineering or SRE lead role, owning large multi-team infrastructure programs end to end in production distributed systems, ML infrastructure, or cloud platforms. You can speak to the outcomes in detail, including where a program slipped and what you did about it. Technical fluency in large-scale serving infrastructure, including request routing and load balancing, autoscaling, capacity planning, cluster orchestration, deployment and rollout, and observability. You know enough to challenge a design, find the real risk, and add value beyond tracking. A working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware (prefill and decode, batching, caching, compute versus memory bandwidth versus interconnect), or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar technical domain quickly. A track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on ambiguous, fast-moving efforts, and of retiring process that has stopped earning its keep. The ability to drive outcomes across organizations you don't manage, with competing priorities and unclear decision ownership. You read people and rooms well, know when to push and when to listen, and earn the trust of senior engineers and researchers. Strong written communication, including plans, reviews, and executive updates that many teams depend on. Low ego and high ownership. You do whatever the program needs, whether that is writing a script, running an incident bridge, or chasing a quota, and you care more about the outcome than about scope or credit. Care about Anthropic's mission and about serving frontier AI safely and reliably. Preferred qualifications Direct experience with LLM or ML inference serving at scale, such as model servers, batching and scheduling, KV caching, quantization, speculative decoding, or multi-model routing. Experience with accelerator infrastructure (GPU, TPU, or Trainium), including cluster bring-up, hardware qualification, or running one workload across more than one accelerator platform. Experience managing capacity across multiple clouds or regions, including demand forecasting, headroom policy, cost modeling, or unit economics for compute-heavy services. Experience with developer productivity, release engineering, or CI/CD at scale, especially for hardware-dependent workloads, and with using engineering metrics to measurably raise velocity. Experience running performance or efficiency programs, with enough grounding in rooflines, kernels, ML compilers (XLA, Triton, Neuron), numerics, or collective communication to reason about trade-offs with the engineers doing the work. Familiarity with Kubernetes-based orchestration and job scheduling. Experience working with research teams and turning their needs into infrastructure requirements. Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, including building automations or agents, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $290,000 — $435,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.

jobs.title: Clinical Oncology Specialist, GU
jobs.description: Territory: Detroit, MI & Indiana Natera is seeking an experienced Clinical Oncology Specialist (COS) to join our specialized Genitourinary (GU) Oncology sales team. This high-impact, tumor-specific role will focus on driving adoption and growth of Signatera™, Natera's personalized, tumor-informed molecular residual disease (MRD) test , across the GU Oncology landscape. Signatera is a circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assay designed to detect molecular residual disease and monitor disease recurrence. Across GU cancers, including bladder, renal cell carcinoma, and testicular cancers, Signatera provides highly specific molecular insights that can help clinicians assess recurrence risk, monitor disease status, and inform individualized patient management strategies. The Clinical Oncology Specialist will serve as a strategic field partner and key representative of Natera Oncology, developing relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and healthcare providers across academic medical centers, integrated delivery networks, hospital systems, and select community oncology practices. This position will have a primary focus on Urologic Oncology, with key call points including Urologic Oncologists, GU Surgical Oncologists, Radiation Oncologists, Medical Oncologists, Pathologists, and other healthcare providers involved in the diagnosis, treatment, and ongoing management of patients with genitourinary cancers. Primary Responsibilities Develop and execute strategic territory business plans to drive Signatera adoption, achieve sales objectives, and maximize market opportunities. Build and strengthen relationships with Urologic Oncologists, GU Surgical Oncologists, Medical Oncologists, Radiation Oncologists, Pathologists, and other key stakeholders across the GU Oncology continuum of care. Drive new account acquisition, expand existing partnerships, and identify growth opportunities within academic medical centers, hospital systems, leading urology practices, and community oncology networks. Educate healthcare providers on Signatera's clinical applications, supporting evidence, and value in the management of GU cancers, including bladder, kidney, and testicular cancers. Develop relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) specializing in GU Oncology, particularly within major academic medical centers and leading urology and oncology practices. Establish expertise in Natera's molecular diagnostics technology, clinical evidence, product offerings, and competitive landscape. Collaborate closely with Natera's Core Oncology Sales team and cross-functional partners to align account strategies and maximize commercial effectiveness. Identify opportunities to expand Signatera adoption through physician education, strategic account development, and multidisciplinary care team engagement. Navigate complex healthcare systems, reimbursement processes, and institutional requirements to support successful product adoption. Partner with internal teams to resolve operational challenges, support account needs, and ensure a positive customer experience. Collaborate with Medical Affairs to support appropriate scientific engagement and KOL development in accordance with company policies. Support the development of institutional care pathways, account-level workflows, and EMR integrations to facilitate testing adoption. Monitor market trends, competitive dynamics, and evolving clinical evidence in GU Oncology to identify opportunities for territory growth. Execute sales and marketing initiatives aligned with regional and national Oncology objectives. Qualifications Bachelor's degree required. Minimum of 5 years of demonstrated sales success within Oncology, Urology, Urologic Oncology, Medical Devices, Molecular Diagnostics, Clinical Diagnostics, or the diagnostic laboratory industry. Experience calling on Urologic Oncologists, GU Surgical Oncologists, Urologists, or other GU Oncology specialists strongly preferred. Experience selling into academic medical centers, integrated healthcare systems, hospital networks, and/or community oncology practices preferred. Demonstrated track record of achieving or exceeding sales goals, developing new markets, and growing complex territories. Experience with molecular diagnostics, precision oncology, or innovative medical technologies preferred. Ability to travel 50–75%, including overnight travel as required. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong understanding of the GU Oncology landscape, including key physician specialties, treatment pathways, and multidisciplinary care models. Knowledge of molecular diagnostics, ctDNA, MRD testing, and precision oncology preferred. Exceptional communication, presentation, relationship-building, and consultative selling skills. Strong business acumen with the ability to identify market opportunities, develop strategic account plans, and execute territory growth initiatives. Ability to establish and maintain trusted relationships with Key Opinion Leaders, physician stakeholders, and healthcare executives. Ability to effectively navigate complex healthcare systems, reimbursement environments, and institutional decision-making processes. Collaborative approach to working with cross-functional teams, including Core Oncology Sales, Marketing, Medical Affairs, and internal support functions. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Self-motivated, results-oriented, and adaptable to a fast-paced, evolving healthcare environment. Commitment to ethical business practices, clinical integrity, and improving patient care. Why Join Natera? Join Natera and play a meaningful role in advancing precision oncology for patients with genitourinary cancers. As a Clinical Oncology Specialist, you will have the opportunity to drive adoption of innovative MRD technology, establish relationships with leading Urologic Oncologists and cancer centers, and expand access to personalized molecular testing. This is an opportunity to help shape the future of GU Oncology while contributing to Natera's continued growth and mission to transform disease management through innovative diagnostics. Compensation & Benefits The total on-target earnings (OTE) package includes: Competitive base salary with uncapped quarterly commissions. Car allowance program. Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). Comprehensive benefits package supporting health, wellness, and career growth. The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. On-target earnings (OTE) represent the total potential income an employee can earn by achieving 100% of their performance goals. It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes. On-target earnings (OTE) $190,000 — $225,000 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @ natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes. For more information: - BBB announcement on job scams - FBI Cyber Crime resource page

jobs.description: Use Your Power for Purpose The Global Clinical Supply (GCS) Interactive Response Technology (IRT) Implementation Analyst is a position within Global Central Operations Network (GCON) GCS Strategic Hubs (GSH) team and will be based in Philippines. The IRT Implementation Analyst will be reporting to the GSH Team Lead in Philippines, with a matrix reporting relationship to the Engagement Leader, IRT Global Oversight Team (IGOT) within Clinical Supply Informatics & Technology (CSIT). GCS manages the execution of supply chain strategies to deliver Investigational Medicinal Product to patients involved in Pfizer’s clinical research trials across the globe. IGOT is a well-established high performing team within Pfizer's GCS unit striving to deliver best in class IRT systems providing randomization and drug management capabilities in support of Pfizer's dynamic investigational product portfolio. The patients we serve are our number one priority and IGOT aims to employ the highest quality standards across our internal and vendor IRT solutions. As part of an innovative clinical supply chain, we routinely challenge the status quo in efforts to optimize our systems and processes. The IRT Implementation Analyst is an individual contributor who performs defined implementation activities under the direction of an accountable IRT Lead, Design Lead, or functional lead. Responsibility and independence will expand progressively based on completion of required training, demonstrated proficiency, and role readiness. This role requires providing support across other global time zones based on business need, specifically from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m Philippine Time or 9:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. Philippine Time (equivalent to 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. U. S. Eastern Time). What You Will Achieve The IRT Implementation Analyst is a new role within the IRT IGOT that will support requirements and system development. The implementation of this dedicated function within IGOT is intended to ensure the delivery of high-quality IRT systems through focused system expertise while improving velocity in support of Pfizer’s evolving portfolio. The IRT Implementation Analyst will go through a robust onboarding and technical training period where they will partner closely with IGOT’s IRT Leads and Design Leads to develop proficiency in conducting preliminary protocol assessments, eliciting protocol requirements, and designing and configuring study builds on Pfizer’s internal IRT system. The IRT Implementation Analyst will support Implementation team members by organizing and facilitating meetings, capturing meeting minutes, creating and reviewing IRT supportive documents, and delivering investigator meeting slides to clinical teams and site personnel. IRT Implementation Analysts will also support line leads in collaborating with study team and supply chain personnel to resolve issues, understand how study requirements are configured and supported post study go-live, and for ongoing studies, be available for guidance on IRT resupply settings and any requisite system amendments. The IRT Implementation Analyst will also learn how quality investigations, Correction Action/ Preventive Action (CAPA) commitments and continuous improvements, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) review and revision activities, support regulatory inspections, and limited duration teams are created and executed. For this position candidates will need to have excellent technical and analytical thinking skills, be a creative problem solver, and have a strong commitment to quality to successfully deliver optimal IRT systems across a diverse and dynamic portfolio Role Responsibilities: Support the delivery plan for IRT configuration and testing activities. Support the elicitation and documentation of system requirements for new and amended studies in partnership with the study team. Support the development and execution of User Acceptance Testing (UAT) test plans. Participate in cross line initiatives, quality investigations, SOP development, and process improvement. Will be trained to create IRT supportive documents and deliver investigator meeting slides to clinical teams and site personnel. Support for Assigned Projects: Aid in the design, delivery, and management of activities related to assigned projects. Participate in study and functional meetings and provide clear updates on assigned activities, risks, actions, and deliverables under the guidance of the accountable IRT Lead, Design Lead, or functional lead Coordinate and execute assigned activities across multiple studies or projects, manage competing priorities, and meet agreed timelines and quality expectations. Use appropriate metrics to measure progress on goals, develop and implement key performance indicators (KPI) to track and measure progress towards strategic goals and ensure value-driven outcomes. Adapt and response quickly to changing business needs and deliver results in challenging first-time situation. Provide timely and actionable insights to stakeholders to support decision-making and strategic planning. Apply approved procedures, standards, and training to resolve routine issues within assigned activities; identify risks, exceptions, or unclear requirements and escalate them promptly to the accountable lead undefined Attend periodic meetings with teams in other global time zones outside of normal work hours. Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements): Associate degree or BA degree in computer science, life science, or business field desired in biopharma industry 1-3 years demonstrated and relevant experience in pharma/biotech and cross-functional team, Possess excellent English language written and verbal communication Interpersonal, collaboration and business partnership capabilities required Comfortable working with a global team, partners, and customers in a change agile environment Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements): Clinical supply chain, project management, business analysis, and/or continuous improvement experience Adaptability to changing priorities and requirements Ability to work in a fast-paced environment Work Location Assignment: Hybrid Pfizer is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity legislation in each jurisdiction in which it operates. jobs.title: Manufacturing Systems Engineer (PLC)
jobs.description: Career Category Engineering Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Manufacturing Systems Engineer I (PLC) What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will provide technical expertise to support the design, maintenance, optimization, and lifecycle management of manufacturing automation systems. You approved implementations within assigned scope, resolve moderate-complexity issues, and collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to improve system reliability, operational performance, and compliance with GMP, Good Engineering Practice (GEP), EHSS, and regulatory requirements. Provide day-to-day automation support, including troubleshooting, incident investigation, system monitoring, change implementation, and coordination with relevant stakeholders. Escalate and work closely with the Senior Manufacturing System Engineer on complex, high-impact, or non-routine issues. Assess, implement, test, deploy, and document automation changes in accordance with applicable SOPs and GMP requirements. Participate in technical discussions and provide technical assessment and advice within their assigned scope; engage the Senior Automation Engineer for complex, high-impact, or non-routine changes. Support technical work and small-to-medium automation projects from design and risk assessment through commissioning, qualification, startup, and handover. Troubleshoot and investigate automation issues; prepare technical reports; implement technical solutions and CAPA actions; and identify recurring issues for improvement. Escalate complex issues to the Senior Automation Engineer. Identify, develop and implement continuous improvement opportunities to improve automation-system reliability, efficiency and compliance. Monitor and analyze established metrics; recommend and implement approved improvements. Promote Safety, Quality and Compliance culture and continuous improvement mindset that lead to plant safety, quality and compliance to regulatory requirement Support audits and inspections and participate in discussions within their assigned technical scope. Prepare and review technical specifications, test plans, change records, implementation plans, contingency measures, and as-built documentation. Coordinate with Manufacturing, Quality, Maintenance, Process Engineering, IT/OT, EHSS and external service providers to execute operational activities, changes and technical issue resolution. Share technical knowledge and provide day-to-day guidance to junior engineers and contractors within their area of expertise. All listed tasks and responsibilities are deemed as essential functions to this position; however, business conditions may require reasonable accommodations for additional tasks and responsibilities. What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. Master’s degree OR Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of directly related experience OR Associate’s degree and/or 4 years of directly related experience OR High school diploma / GED and 6 years of directly related experience Preferred 4+ years’ experience in manufacturing automation, particularly in biotechnology or pharmaceutical industries Preferred 4+ years' experience supporting and maintaining Siemens PLCs, DDCs, Building Management Systems (BMS), and Quality Environmental Monitoring Systems (QEMS) in a manufacturing or industrial environment. Working knowledge of Rockwell and Siemens PLC/HMI hardware, lifecycle management, control logic, HMI/SCADA systems, Microsoft SQL Database, industrial networks, field instrumentation, and environmental monitoring equipment. Experience troubleshooting system faults, assessing operational impact, and coordinating corrective actions with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, and external service providers. Experience with utility skid equipment such as HVAC, Cooling Tower, Chiller, RO, Clean Steam and Waste Treatment system. Experience applying GMP requirements, including change control, risk assessment, testing, documentation, data integrity, computerized system validation, industrial standard (21 CFR Part 11, GAMP) and deviation or CAPA support. Experience supporting or delivering automation projects involving BMS, Siemens PLCs, or QEMS, from requirements and design through testing, commissioning, handover, and documentation. Strong communication, planning, and collaboration skills. Working knowledge of EHSS requirements Your selection for this role will be subject to fulfilling the medical requirements of this job scope. If so, you will be informed of the medical check(s) that you may need to undergo. All medical related expenses incurred from this medical check shall be borne by the company. What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers competitive and comprehensive Total Rewards Plans that are aligned with local industry standards. Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team. careers.amgen.com As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of diverse, ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease. Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other basis protected by applicable law. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. .

Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website. Consulting is changing, and we’re not like other firms. Launched in 2019, Veeva Business Consulting has grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep domain knowledge with innovative technology to help Life Sciences companies work in a more efficient and connected way. We are growing aggressively as we look towards 2030. Our Business Consulting team is focused on speeding drug development, launching treatments more effectively, and shaping the best engagement for our customers. We are seeking great people to help shape the future of the industry with the world’s leading software, data, AI, and expertise at their back. The Role We are hiring recent university graduates to grow the next generation of consultants through our Business Consultant Development Program (BCDP). We believe in pushing high potential people to achieve excellence. Our program is specifically designed to provide a challenging environment to learn quickly and deliver value early. You will collaborate with experienced team members on customer-facing engagements to create high-impact business solutions. In our structured 20 month program, we equip you with the resources to develop the core consulting skills, deep domain expertise, and leadership foundation for long-term career success at Veeva. BCDP spans five core practice areas: Analytics, Commercial, Content, R&D, and Quality. As an Associate Consultant you will align to one of those practices, allowing you to build targeted industry expertise. You will be asked to choose your preferred practice in the application process. You can learn more about our practices and the work we do here. The anticipated start date is September 2027.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Business Consultant - Life Sciences Consulting — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Veeva Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Business Consultant - Life Sciences Consulting opportunity with Veeva at Veeva.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
